newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. mother killed by 'flesh-eating' bacteria.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. mother killed by 'flesh-eating' bacteria.

text.p: An outbreak of a rare "flesh-eating" bacteria has claimed the life of a mother who gave birth last month and infected two more women who were in the same maternity ward, according to local news reports.

The unnamed woman died on Friday at Strong Memorial Hospital, and although the cause of her death remains under investigation, family members told Saturday's Rochester Democrat and Chronicle that she had "necrotizing fasciitis" -- popularly known as the "flesh-eating bug."
Hospital officials refused to give any details, but confirmed they were treating several patients with Group A streptococcus.

Spokesman Robert Loeb would say only that Strong Memorial Hospital was treating a "cluster" of patients with Group A strep. He refused to identify the dead woman, who he said gave birth to a healthy child by Ceasarean section last month.

The source of the outrbeak has not been identified and New York State Health Department is sending a team of medical investigators to the hospital on Monday to try to determine whether the source was internal or external.
A maternity ward technician is among those being treated at the hospital.
Officials are limiting visitors to obstetric and gynecological patients and all visitors are being screened for symptoms of the disease, which include a sore throat and fever.

Flesh-eating bugs, which killed three heroin addicts in San Francisco last April, are similar to the common "strep throat", and scientists blame mutations of bacteria into deadly strains on overuse of antibiotics.
